'''Libera Trevisani Levi-Civita''' (17 May 1890 – 11 December 1973) was an Italian [[mathematician]] born in [[Verona]].<ref>[http://scienzaa2voci.unibo.it/biografie/138-trevisani-levi-civita-libera An Italian biography of Libera Trevisani Levi-Civita]</ref>

==Biography==
Libera Trevisani earned her classical lyceum A levels in 1908 at the "Bernardino Telesio" Lyceum in [[Cosenza]]. In the 1908–1909 academic year, she matriculated at the [[University of Padova]].<ref>Archivio storico dell’Università di Padova, Registro della carriera scolastica, "Libera Trevisani".</ref>

In 1912, she graduated at the University of Padova, under the guidance of the mathematician [[Tullio Levi-Civita]], with a thesis titled ''Sul moto medio dei nodi nel problema dei tre corpi'' ("About the average motion within the three body problem").<ref>{{MathGenealogy |id=165082}}</ref> This thesis extended Levi-Civita's researches on the average asymptotic motion existence, for a point represented by the generic solution of a linear system with periodic coefficients, to the [[Three-body problem|problem of the three bodies]], whenever this is referred to the moon theory. The results achieved by Trevisani were so satisfactory that her mentor decided to present them to 28 April 1912 meeting at the [[Istituto veneto di scienze, lettere ed arti]] (Veneto's Institute of sciences, letters and arts). The note was published in the ''Atti'' (Records) in the same year.<ref>Sul moto medio dei nodi nel problema dei tre corpi, «Atti dell'Istituto veneto di scienze, lettere ed arti», LXXI, 1912, pp. 1089–1137.</ref>

In April 1914, the young Libera Trevisani married her mentor, Tullio Levi-Civita.<ref name="Goodstein"/>{{rp|115–117}}

In 1944 she was elected president of the reinstated {{ill|FILDIS|it}} (''Federazione Italiana Laureate e Diplomate di Istituti Superiori'' – Federation of Italian Graduated Women in Higher Education)<ref>{{cite web|title=F.I.L.D.I.S.|url=http://www.fildisitalia.it/|accessdate=14 July 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170709204755/http://www.fildisitalia.it/|archive-date=9 July 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> which had been dissolved in 1935 by the [[Fascist Italy (1922–1943)|fascist regime]]. She remained in office until 1953 and carried on institutional initiatives aimed at the empowerment of women and the protection of women's rights.

In 1945 Libera retrieved Susanna Silberstein<ref>[https://www.hakeillah.com/2_20_24.htm In Memoria di Susanna Silberstein] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220730165634/https://www.hakeillah.com/2_20_24.htm |date=30 July 2022 }} ''Ha Keillah, LUGLIO 2022  ANNO XLVII - 234 TAMMUZ 5782''</ref> from the Florentine convent where her parents had placed her just before they were rounded up by the Nazis in 1943, and she later adopted her.<ref name="Goodstein">{{cite book
 | last = Goodstein
 | first = Judith R.
 |author-link = Judith R. Goodstein
 | title = Einstein's Italian mathematicians : Ricci, Levi-Civita, and the birth of general relativity
